tools.name: rows
tools.description: Page through the rows of a table: a table_id from fetch, upload_confirm, wrangle or sql_query. Returns rows page*page_size .. (page+1)*page_size-1, the total row_count and has_more (false on the last page). Nothing is downloaded or cleaned again: only the requested slice is read. Also reads a wrangl

tools.name: wrangle

tools.description: Finish an upload: once the file is on the `upload_page` (or a shell PUT it), this cleans it into a private scratch table -- the same clean, typed result as fetch. Returns the table_id and when it expires, the schema, row count, issues and a page of rows. The file's own name is known from the upload;

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "wrangle" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?channel=ch-0S999H2GZ0KP7" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, upload_request, upload_confirm · Private data: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, export, upload_request, upload_confirm · Public sink: upload_request, upload_confirm · Destructive: fetch, wrangle, sql_query, export.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, upload_request, upload_confirm · Private data: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, export, upload_request, upload_confirm · Public sink: upload_request, upload_confirm · Destructive: fetch, wrangle, sql_query, export

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
